definitions.explanation: Traditional Japanese martial arts that emphasize both physical technique and spiritual/moral development, including judo, kendo, karate, and aikido.

examples.japanese: {武道|ぶどう}を{通|とお}じて{精神|せいしん}を{鍛|きた}える。
examples.english: I train my spirit through martial arts.

examples.japanese: {日本|にほん}の{武道|ぶどう}は{世界|せかい}で{人気|にんき}がある。
examples.english: Japanese martial arts are popular around the world.

examples.japanese: {武道|ぶどう}{館|かん}で{剣道|けんどう}の{試合|しあい}が{行|おこな}われた。
examples.english: A kendo tournament was held at the martial arts hall.

notes:
{武道|ぶどう} refers to Japanese martial arts as a discipline — emphasizing spiritual and moral development alongside physical technique.

TYPES OF {武道|ぶどう}:
- {柔道|じゅうどう}: judo
- {剣道|けんどう}: kendo (sword fighting)
- {空手|からて}: karate
- {合気道|あいきどう}: aikido
- {弓道|きゅうどう}: kyudo (archery)
- {相撲|すもう}: sumo

COMMON COMPOUNDS:
- {武道|ぶどう}{館|かん}: martial arts hall
- {武道|ぶどう}{家|か}: martial artist
- {武道|ぶどう}{精神|せいしん}: martial arts spirit

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {武道|ぶどう}: martial arts as a way of life ({道|みち} = "the way")
- {武術|ぶじゅつ}: martial arts as combat technique
- {格闘技|かくとうぎ}: fighting sports (broader, includes non-Japanese arts)

HOMOPHONE:
Same reading as {葡萄|ぶどう} (grapes) — different kanji and meaning.
